help chi
Subject: chi
=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

In Categories: Magic, Skill

Usage:
  - invoke <spell #>
  - invoke <spell #> <target>
  - invoke <alias>
  - invoke <alias> <target>


The "chi" skill is available only to the Monk class. It is designed to provide minor buffs to the monk class, such as giving them with a weak haste spell. Since most of the monk's damage comes from physical damage in the form of their martial arts ability, the damage dealing abilities in the chi skill are negligible and designed to be used as a last resort or to aid in the task of leveling the skill. One of the greatest boons of the chi skill to the monk, is the ability to restore fatigue, the resourced used by their martial arts skill. To see which chi spells are available to you at the moment, use the command; spells. As you increase your level in chi, you'll learn new ones, so keep checking! Each time you cast a spell, it will use up some mana. Mana regenerates slowly over time so manage it carefully!

See also: disguise, monk, skill, alias, invoke

A large open arch leads eastward into the main billiards area. [Belladonna's Billiards]
Entranced by a large elegant thatched and latticed arch, the Peacock's hall of billiards is famous for its lavish and sultry atmosphere. Stationed across the red-carpeted game-patterned floor are several billiards tables covered in bright green velvet, and they form a straight line down the hall to the eastern end which boasts of a large stone fireplace, and several tall bay windows which look out over the eastern section of the inn grounds. Along the entire red brick and mortar windowless western wall is a long open marble-topped bar, which is well-stocked with liquors and ales and wines and hundreds of crystal drinking glasses and goblets, on mirrored shelves directly behind the bar. The center bar mirror behind the hovering fae bartender, is finely-flecked with formal gold lettering which reads, "~There but by the grace of honor go I into battle, and by the same virtue I return to celebrate its victory.~" At each ornate, intricate game table stands a pleasant, well-dressed, beefy Duskwen pit boss. There to keep the peace, fairness, and honesty of each game, they are alert, and ever-watchful for signs of cheaters, thieves, and miscreants. Built into the northern wall is a small riser, stage, and bard section attached to the eastern side of it. A Silvarin bard sits in the small bard section idly tuning his amberwood viol, and smoking a tightly-rolled thin black cigar. A glittery sign sitting on a wood tripod on center stage reads, "The next burlesque show featuring Belladonna's fine females begins in: [one hour]".

[Red Peacock-Main Hall]
At the end of the grand hallway, several clear-paned, oak-framed window doors lead to an outdoor balcony which overlooks the northern part of the Rose Peacock property. Gazing out you can see rows of well-pruned fruit trees forming a small lush meadow around a thin exposed rivulet which has dead-ended into a shallow clear pond. A mother goose leads her small gaggle of babies skimming along expertly on its otherwise calm surface. To the east in this grand hall is an open arch which leads to the main poker area. Hung from the two story high ceiling by black chains, is a twenty five foot long gold-plated ceramic cast model of a wingless crouching imperial dragon. His serpentine spiked and finned tail and body curves in oval circles up to a massive horned, fanged dragon head, which opens its maw and spews a gold-plated ceramic fire storm above your head. Two antique gold-plated, red velvet plush thrones sit commandingly along the western wall, separated by an ornate gold-leafed pulpit. The pulpit itself bears an inscribed gold plaque which reads, "These are the same thrones owned and sat upon by the last Emperor and Empress of the long vanquished Galatean empire. By virtue of luck, circumstance, and careful trading, they have come to rest here, and on display for all to see. Please DO NOT sit in them. ~Management" The artifacts are roped off with red velvet ropes and gold chains.

[The Red Peacock]
The main foyer of the Peacock is spacious and elegant with no expense spared. Ten foot bay windows line the western and southern walls, and provide a clear view of the front entrance and side lot respectively. The pearl white lace curtains are hung on finely polished brass rods, drawn tightly, and tied in the middle with gold ropes. In the center of the two-story high vaulted ceiling hangs a massive cascading crystal chandelier, its millions of sharp points blazing brightly throughout the grand entrance hall. Tall tropical broad-leaf plants are potted in fine brass urns, and placed strategically throughout the foyer area. The front reception desk is centrally located along the northern wall, and several hotel-uniformed Fae buzz quickly back and forth at each receiving pulpit, taking names, reservations, answering messengers, and directing patrons to and fro throughout the swanky inn. Two well-dressed and uniformed burly Duskwen bellhops stand resolutely by the broad, glass-paned front doors awaiting a tip, and a chance to take a high roller and his gear to the high roller's suite. In the very center of the highly polished marble floor is a giant circular, rotating map of the Isles of Aedin. Turning constantly, the floor map is roped off with black leather ropes, and tethered with brass chains to waist-high brass poles positioned all the way around it. Several patrons gather around the map, marveling at its size, accuracy, and apparent self-turning ability. On each side of the northern front desk are large spacious hallways, well-lit with cascading black cast-iron chandeliers that hang from the two-story high vaulted ceilings, and light your way further into the heart of The Rose Peacock, famous for its grand display, fine dining, fast gambling, excellent service, lavish lifestyle, and wealthy clientele.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

Built into the northern wall is a small riser, stage, and bard section attached to the eastern side of it. A pair of formally-dressed wealthy Akathri keep time with the music in the form of sweeping, dextrous hops, jumps, twists and other popular dance moves in front of the small stage. At one poker table the game is getting heated, and a small crowd has formed around it, urging the gamblers on, and applauding and cheering when a hand is well-played or won, and dying down to a soft murmur while the next big hand is dealt, and carefully played out.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

The area is illuminated.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

The area is illuminated.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

[The Red Peacock]
The main foyer of the Peacock is spacious and elegant with no expense spared. Ten foot bay windows line the western and southern walls, and provide a clear view of the front entrance and side lot respectively. The pearl white lace curtains are hung on finely polished brass rods, drawn tightly, and tied in the middle with gold ropes. In the center of the two-story high vaulted ceiling hangs a massive cascading crystal chandelier, its millions of sharp points blazing brightly throughout the grand entrance hall. Tall tropical broad-leaf plants are potted in fine brass urns, and placed strategically throughout the foyer area. The front reception desk is centrally located along the northern wall, and several hotel-uniformed Fae buzz quickly back and forth at each receiving pulpit, taking names, reservations, answering messengers, and directing patrons to and fro throughout the swanky inn. Two well-dressed and uniformed burly Duskwen bellhops stand resolutely by the broad, glass-paned front doors awaiting a tip, and a chance to take a high roller and his gear to the high roller's suite. In the very center of the highly polished marble floor is a giant circular, rotating map of the Isles of Aedin. Turning constantly, the floor map is roped off with black leather ropes, and tethered with brass chains to waist-high brass poles positioned all the way around it. Several patrons gather around the map, marveling at its size, accuracy, and apparent self-turning ability. On each side of the northern front desk are large spacious hallways, well-lit with cascading black cast-iron chandeliers that hang from the two-story high vaulted ceilings, and light your way further into the heart of The Rose Peacock, famous for its grand display, fine dining, fast gambling, excellent service, lavish lifestyle, and wealthy clientele.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

The area is illuminated.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

The area is illuminated.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

[The Red Peacock]
The main foyer of the Peacock is spacious and elegant with no expense spared. Ten foot bay windows line the western and southern walls, and provide a clear view of the front entrance and side lot respectively. The pearl white lace curtains are hung on finely polished brass rods, drawn tightly, and tied in the middle with gold ropes. In the center of the two-story high vaulted ceiling hangs a massive cascading crystal chandelier, its millions of sharp points blazing brightly throughout the grand entrance hall. Tall tropical broad-leaf plants are potted in fine brass urns, and placed strategically throughout the foyer area. The front reception desk is centrally located along the northern wall, and several hotel-uniformed Fae buzz quickly back and forth at each receiving pulpit, taking names, reservations, answering messengers, and directing patrons to and fro throughout the swanky inn. Two well-dressed and uniformed burly Duskwen bellhops stand resolutely by the broad, glass-paned front doors awaiting a tip, and a chance to take a high roller and his gear to the high roller's suite. In the very center of the highly polished marble floor is a giant circular, rotating map of the Isles of Aedin. Turning constantly, the floor map is roped off with black leather ropes, and tethered with brass chains to waist-high brass poles positioned all the way around it. Several patrons gather around the map, marveling at its size, accuracy, and apparent self-turning ability. On each side of the northern front desk are large spacious hallways, well-lit with cascading black cast-iron chandeliers that hang from the two-story high vaulted ceilings, and light your way further into the heart of The Rose Peacock, famous for its grand display, fine dining, fast gambling, excellent service, lavish lifestyle, and wealthy clientele.

[East Ballroom]
The grand and spacious ballroom doubles as a banquet hall, as well as a convention hall, as evidenced by the large folded rectangular banquet tables, and padded folding chairs neatly stacked at the back of the room. Instead of a northern wall, a riser and small stage are in its place, complete with front curtains, a grand open-lidded harpsichord, and a moveable pulpit. For the right price, a large group or organization can reserve this hall for their own parties, banquets, dances, as well as performers and live stage shows. Along the southern wall is a large open serving window, with a brushed silver counter top, which leads to a small grill and kitchen. Under the food serving window is a white linen-covered banquet table, fully stocked with sparkling clean dishes, plates, eating ware, utensils, drinking glasses, crystal wine goblets, ale mugs, and white folded linen napkins. Underneath the tall bay windows in the eastern wall are several well-stocked walnut-paneled portable mini bars. The entire red brick and mortar western wall is windowless, and covered with signed and autographed portraits of famous patrons and performers who have come and gone from, and stayed within the elegant walls of the Eastern Horn of Urda. The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. This open ballroom looks like it could accommodate about two hundred patrons comfortably.

[The Red Peacock]
The main foyer of the Peacock is spacious and elegant with no expense spared. Ten foot bay windows line the western and southern walls, and provide a clear view of the front entrance and side lot respectively. The pearl white lace curtains are hung on finely polished brass rods, drawn tightly, and tied in the middle with gold ropes. In the center of the two-story high vaulted ceiling hangs a massive cascading crystal chandelier, its millions of sharp points blazing brightly throughout the grand entrance hall. Tall tropical broad-leaf plants are potted in fine brass urns, and placed strategically throughout the foyer area. The front reception desk is centrally located along the northern wall, and several hotel-uniformed Fae buzz quickly back and forth at each receiving pulpit, taking names, reservations, answering messengers, and directing patrons to and fro throughout the swanky inn. Two well-dressed and uniformed burly Duskwen bellhops stand resolutely by the broad, glass-paned front doors awaiting a tip, and a chance to take a high roller and his gear to the high roller's suite. In the very center of the highly polished marble floor is a giant circular, rotating map of the Isles of Aedin. Turning constantly, the floor map is roped off with black leather ropes, and tethered with brass chains to waist-high brass poles positioned all the way around it. Several patrons gather around the map, marveling at its size, accuracy, and apparent self-turning ability. On each side of the northern front desk are large spacious hallways, well-lit with cascading black cast-iron chandeliers that hang from the two-story high vaulted ceilings, and light your way further into the heart of The Rose Peacock, famous for its grand display, fine dining, fast gambling, excellent service, lavish lifestyle, and wealthy clientele.

[East Horn Main Gate]
Two square pillars of red brick and mortar stand twenty feet high on each side of the black, cast-iron elaborate two-door gate. The pillars solidly connect the entrance gates to the ten foot high red brick and mortar walls which surround the East Horn entirely, and keep it safe within. The gate itself is twenty five feet high, with an arch at the top, which is nicely decorated with black, cast-iron vines, flowers, and the words "East Horn of Urda" in the center of the arch. The gate is heavily guarded by well-armed sentries and security patrollers, as the middle-to-high class citizens who live here can afford such security. Merchants, nobles, aristocrats, city leaders, temple leaders, and others of established wealth and rank live within the walls of the East Horn of Urda. A large deep-stained oak sign here reads, "Welcome to the East Horn", followed by, "Go in peace", and it is finely etched with grape vine designs, laden with ripe grapes. A knight in shining armor stops you politely at the gate, reminding you that all crime is forbidden here upon penalty severe, and then ushers you inside before returning to his posted guard.

[East Horn Main Gate]
Two square pillars of red brick and mortar stand twenty feet high on each side of the black, cast-iron elaborate two-door gate. The pillars solidly connect the entrance gates to the ten foot high red brick and mortar walls which surround the East Horn entirely, and keep it safe within. The gate itself is twenty five feet high, with an arch at the top, which is nicely decorated with black, cast-iron vines, flowers, and the words "East Horn of Urda" in the center of the arch. The gate is heavily guarded by well-armed sentries and security patrollers, as the middle-to-high class citizens who live here can afford such security. Merchants, nobles, aristocrats, city leaders, temple leaders, and others of established wealth and rank live within the walls of the East Horn of Urda. [The Red Peacock]
The main foyer of the Peacock is spacious and elegant with no expense spared. Ten foot bay windows line the western and southern walls, and provide a clear view of the front entrance and side lot respectively. The pearl white lace curtains are hung on finely polished brass rods, drawn tightly, and tied in the middle with gold ropes. In the center of the two-story high vaulted ceiling hangs a massive cascading crystal chandelier, its millions of sharp points blazing brightly throughout the grand entrance hall. Tall tropical broad-leaf plants are potted in fine brass urns, and placed strategically throughout the foyer area. The front reception desk is centrally located along the northern wall, and several hotel-uniformed Fae buzz quickly back and forth at each receiving pulpit, taking names, reservations, answering messengers, and directing patrons to and fro throughout the swanky inn. Two well-dressed and uniformed burly Duskwen bellhops stand resolutely by the broad, glass-paned front doors awaiting a tip, and a chance to take a high roller and his gear to the high roller's suite. In the very center of the highly polished marble floor is a giant circular, rotating map of the Isles of Aedin. Turning constantly, the floor map is roped off with black leather ropes, and tethered with brass chains to waist-high brass poles positioned all the way around it. Several patrons gather around the map, marveling at its size, accuracy, and apparent self-turning ability. On each side of the northern front desk are large spacious hallways, well-lit with cascading black cast-iron chandeliers that hang from the two-story high vaulted ceilings, and light your way further into the heart of The Rose Peacock, famous for its grand display, fine dining, fast gambling, excellent service, lavish lifestyle, and wealthy clientele.

The ballroom floor is highly-varnished slats of walnut and oak, ornately and finely connected together in different mosaic patterns. Incorrect syntax. Type help shop for assistance.

help shop
Subject: shop
=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

In Categories: Shopping

Usage:
  - shop list
  - shop list <category name>
  - shop buy <item #>
  - shop sell <item>
  - shop examine <item #>
  - shop appraise <item>
  - shop refill <item>
  - shop repair <item>
  - shop claim
  - shop contact <player> <message>
  - shop store <item>
  - shop fetch <item #>
  - shop fetch list
  - shop unlock <item>
  - shop hours
  - shop refill <item>
  - shop heal


Shopping, a girl's happy dream and a guy's nightmare. In Aedin, however, it can be fun and easy, as well as extremely useful. Shops are all over the world of Aedin, they can sell just about anything, from fancy clothes to deadly weapons. Most shops can be found within cities, these often sell items needed by the average adventurer. Armor, weapons, restorative potions... Just about anything you could need.

Nearly all shops charge for their goods and services of course, however there are one or two in the Travers training town that cater to the new adventurer. These - the Human Trading Company Emporium (through the door in Travers' Main Square) and Jeebz' Diskownt Markit (southeast, west, south, then through the door) - offer cheaply made gear designed for the needs of the non-discriminating newcomer for free or extremely discounted prices. To see what goods a shop might offer, use the command SHOP LIST, or you can narrow your search by entering the category of item you're looking for. For example, if you are looking specifically for all blade-type weapons sold in the shop you could enter SHOP LIST BLADES. The categories are: Blades | Thrusts | Polearms | Bow | Blunts | Dual Wield | Throwing | Ammo | Lightsource | Shield | Armor | Runestone | Clothing | Container . To purchase an item you can use the command SHOP BUY <item #>. If you're interested in seeing more details about an item in the shop's inventory, use the command SHOP EXAMINE <item #>

In addition to the obvious goods a shop might offer, some shops offer special services for a fee. These can include storage, contacting anther player, repairs to a damaged item, refilling an empty quiver of arrows or stack of thrown weapons, unlocking a locked box, appraising an item in your inventory, or buying an item you no longer want to keep. Keep in mind that not all shops offer all services. 

Shops that offer repair services (often smithies of some kind) are also usually able to refill an empty quiver or stack of thrown weapons. To repair a damaged item while in a shop that offers that service, use the command SHOP REPAIR <item>. Repairing takes time and money, but once it's done you can pick up your newly fixed item with the command SHOP CLAIM. Refilling is similar, you'll use the command SHOP REFILL <item> to refill empty quivers or thrown-type weapons, this is an instant service. Keep in mind, however, that most items can only be repaired or refilled so many times, while others cannot be repaired or refilled at all.

It is often the magical stores that offer the contact service, though some taverns and a few scribe shops have been known to take in the business. This allows a player to instantly and privately contact any other player currently in-game over any distance. It does, of course, cost money, but it is a valuable service. To use this function while in a shop that offers it, use the command SHOP CONTACT <player name> <message>.

Some shops keep a skilled locksmith on staff. These shops can unlock any locked box, but they do charge a hefty price for the service. It is often more safe for the coin purse to track down a locksmith player. But if this isn't possible, you can use the command SHOP UNLOCK <item> while in a lockpicking shop to access this service. 

Almost all shops are willing to appraise the value of an item you have - they'll even do it for free! -, even if they aren't willing to buy. However, if you do stumble across a shop that is willing to buy your old junk, you'll find you can make a decent profit. To use the appraise function you'll use the command SHOP APPRAISE <item>, while to sell to a shop you'll use SHOP SELL <item>.

One of the most useful - and rare - types of shops are those willing to store your items. They charge a decent rate, but the service they offer is valuable. Rather than having to throw away that treasured trophy because it's to heavy to cart around, you can leave it safely locked away in a shop's vault. Each time you deposit an item to be stored (up to a maximum of 50 items), the shop will charge you a crown. In addition, the shop will charge a monthly fee. When in a shop that offers the storage service, you can use the commands SHOP STORE <item> to store an item, SHOP FETCH LIST to see what items you have stored there, and SHOP FETCH <item #> to withdraw an item from the shop's vault.

The final kind of shop is the healing store. They offer full service healing for a reasonable price. To have all hp, ftg, mana, and psi points restored, you may use the command SHOP HEAL.

One last thing to keep in mind while going shopping in Aedin, is that not all shops are open all hours. Many of the necessary shops will remain open at all hours (like the shops in Travers) but others will open and close based on in-game time. To see what hours a shop is open use the command SHOP HOURS. Some shops are also designed to cater to a certain type of clientele. Some will only sell to members of specific races, religons, or classes. 

Happy shopping!


See also: whisper, bank, say, inventory, contact, vinculum, money, open, wolfsong

[Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. Its feathers look almost like scales in the flickering torchlight, and for just a moment, the image of the bird is replaced by a sight of a terrifying black scaled dragon, its yellowed talons reaching for the unwary adventurer.

The area is illuminated.

[Hidden Shadowy Alcove]
The air in this narrow room seems compressed and tight, almost as if it were made of thousands of tiny needles ready to pierce flesh and bone. [Portal Room]
The world shifts and turns violently and suddenly a small room materializes from the nothingness. The walls of the apparently underground room are rough and natural, and the air is stale and still. The only things of note in this small room are two portals, a red portal that seems to lead back up to the true Cathedral is framed by a pair of ordinary candles in sconces, and a sickly looking green portal that leads further into the depths. The candleholders beside the green portal are hanging on the walls strangely, the candles are facing downward and the flames flicker toward the floor.

The area is illuminated.

[Twisted Head Priest's Office]
A swirling green portal takes up the entire back wall of this office, as it spins the air around it seems to bend and distort. The rest of the room seems bare except for smoking torches hung around the walls. Like the candles in the portal room, the flames miraculously burn downward. Overhead a large oak desk hanging upside-down, hopefully nailed securely in place. Papers are scattered across its surface, and an inkwell sits uncorked with a feather quill sitting nearby, it seems as if gravity has no hold over the desk or anything else on the ceiling, including a rug that is an exact color inverted copy of the rug from the Priest's office. A faint breeze emanates from the portal, scattering loose papers across the oak desk, some of the fragile papers blow off the surface and fall upward toward the roof.

The area is illuminated.

In this room you see: Bjeorn the Galirrim,  Primum the Seraphim,  Vynter the Silvarin
Obvious exits are: twisting sickly green passage, blackened doorway

A single, massive column of light descends from above to bathe Bjeorn in a holy glow. As the light fades, a shimmer is left in Bjeorn's eyes.

[Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. Its feathers look almost like scales in the flickering torchlight, and for just a moment, the image of the bird is replaced by a sight of a terrifying black scaled dragon, its yellowed talons reaching for the unwary adventurer.

The area is illuminated.

In this room you see: Bjeorn the Galirrim,  Primum the Seraphim,  Vynter the Silvarin

The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. Its feathers look almost like scales in the flickering torchlight, and for just a moment, the image of the bird is replaced by a sight of a terrifying black scaled dragon, its yellowed talons reaching for the unwary adventurer.

The area is illuminated.

[Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. Its feathers look almost like scales in the flickering torchlight, and for just a moment, the image of the bird is replaced by a sight of a terrifying black scaled dragon, its yellowed talons reaching for the unwary adventurer.

[Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. [Twisted Cathedral Altar]
In a perverted twist on the altar in the true cathedral above, a massive white-veined black marble altar dominates the space. A thick dark liquid runs in a constant cascade in a fountain on the top of the altar, and a thick reddish mist hovers over the liquid in the bottom basin. The coppery scent of blood permeates the area, suggesting that the liquid in the fountain is the heart blood of dozens of daily sacrifices.

The area is illuminated.

In this room you see: Bjeorn the Galirrim,  Primum the Seraphim,  Vynter the Silvarin

[Twisted Cathedral West Wing]
Rows and rows of rough wooden pews line the ceiling, but what lines the walls is more eye-catching. Bubbling and simmering neon potions cover the tabletops. [Twisted Cathedral East Wing]
The floor arches downward toward the center of the massive cathedral and the lining it tiles are scuffed and scraped, but it is more intact than the ceiling in the above room. It is a scene of the open sky. A massive bird, its wings outstretched, takes up the center of the mosaic. In its beak it holds a twisting knot made of sun-bleached rowan wood. The image of the bird on the true cathedral's ceiling would likely be white if it was still intact, but here it is black. [Bridge]
The bridge over the river is a marvel of engineering. Columns made entirely of river stones support the massive cypress beams, each hewn from a single tree. Broad oak planks span the space between each beam with only the smallest of gaps between each plank. [Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.

In this room are: moss-covered green marble altar
Obvious exits are: small path

[Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.

In this room are: moss-covered green marble altar
Obvious exits are: small path

[Temple of the Eyranas]
Amazingly the interior of the temple is teaming with life. Birds fly freely amongst the tall trees and shrubs which give the appearance of the outside instead of in. Small animals scurry across the ground in an almost permanent state of play. A large fountain set in the center of the area spouts water high into the air which then settles back into the fountain without even the smallest splash. Statues of the Goddess's lie scattered among the various ponds and gardens of the temple. A small grassy pasture free of any growth takes its place on the northeastern side of the temple which sits beneath a beautiful green, moss covered altar. A gaggle of bushes trimmed to portray letters spells out the word "Life" in the northwestern corner of the temple. A small path that leads through some thick overgrowth to the west provides passage to another room. To the south an overgrown arch provides exit back to the street.

The area is illuminated.

In this room are: moss-covered green marble altar
Obvious exits are: small path
